text:
alex: quick question about a follow-on to the sideplane RFC: if we run local control agents in customer VPCs, how do we handle egress IPs for callbacks when customers require allowlists?
nisha: two pragmatic modes: (A) preserve source IP by routing via a customer-facing ENI (no SNAT), or (B) SNAT at our regional relay and present a stable egress IP. Both have tradeoffs on ops/cost/failover.
linus: src-preserve is best for strict IP allowlists but needs per-tenant ENI lifecycle, route propagation, and careful failover across AZs/regions. brittle unless dedicated.
olivia: pinning per-tenant ENI/EIP will scale poorly cost-wise. can we reduce blast radius with a shared static IP pool?
nisha: yes: shared pool per region + X-Redwood-Tenant header for app-level routing. solves many app-level cases but won't satisfy network allowlists.
alex: proposal summary: default = regional SNAT. Support opt-in src-preserve for enterprise/dedicated customers (reserved ENI/EIP or equivalent). Offer shared-static pool as intermediate tier. Hybrid: prefer local src-preserve when ENI available, otherwise fallback to shared-static + header, with metrics.
infra-bot: perf-note: per-tenant NAT adds ~0.7-0.9ms p50. cost-note: EIP/NAT hours significant; creating cost ticket for numbers.
linus: failover concern: if sideplane withdraws prefix, traffic will shift to regional relay and lose src-preserve. need soft-handoff to avoid blackholes.
alex: agree. implement withdraw grace-window (30s) + active health-probed path switch. add sequence diagrams and a test harness simulating peering loss.
olivia: rollout plan: feature-flag sideplane egress modes, beta with 5 pilot tenants, default remains regional SNAT. deliver docs, pricing, and ops-runbook before GA.
nisha: add tenant config field egress_mode: ["regional-snat","shared-static","src-preserve"] surfaced in UI and audit logs.
linus: test matrix: allowlist acceptance test, peering-loss SLO test, metrics: fallback_count, pinned_eni_count, shared_pool_util. Include chaos test for withdraw window.
alex: action items: linus -> spike BGP/route-prop options (due 3d), infra -> cost projection + INFRA ticket, olivia -> rollout plan and docs (due 7d). i'll open RFC follow-up with diagrams.
infra-bot: created INFRA-5234 "sideplane egress modes: cost & failover spike"
all: acked.
